title: Auth telemetry & graceful rekey patterns for SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Anika Sharma
description: Goal: define and implement a cross-language pattern for telemetry-driven, graceful rekey (token rotation) inside Redwood SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Focus areas: (1) streaming connection rekey without dropping user streams, (2) short-lived SSO token refresh ergonomics for enterprise customers, (3) auth-related telemetry and correlation IDs for debugging and incident response, (4) clear guidance for local dev and private deployments (KMS/HSM considerations). This ticket produces design docs, SDK surface proposals, and a PoC implementation in at least one SDK with testable examples. Constraints: need to work with existing hosted API and Dedicated/Private modes, support sidecar and sidecar-less deployment models, maintain no-credential-leak promises for log/telemetry, and avoid adding high-latency blocking operations to hot token paths.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and SDK owners
SDK API proposal with minimal breaking surface for Python/TS/Go (examples included)
PoC in TypeScript SDK that performs in-band streaming rekey without dropping active streams (integration tests pass)
Telemetry emitted for all auth lifecycle events (issue, refresh, failed-refresh, server-initiated rekey) with correlation IDs and sanitized metadata
Guidance doc for local-dev and private deployments covering KMS/HSM and ephemeral credentials
Security review completed and release note drafted for sdks-2025.03
work_notes: 2025-02-10: Kickoff - initial scope agreed. Identified two orthogonal flows: client-initiated refresh (refresh token exchange) and server-initiated rekey (rekey frame over stream).

2025-02-12: Spike results - server can push a rekey frame containing ephemeral token+expiry; clients must support pausing token use for in-flight message completion and then resume with new token. Latency impact measured to be <10ms for pause/resume in PoC network lab.
2025-02-15: Security sync - agreed no raw tokens should appear in telemetry. Only sanitized hashes and TTLs emitted. KMS integration patterns enumerated for private deployments.

2025-02-18: API proposals drafted for three SDKs. Key ergonomic decisions: (a) provide an AuthProvider interface that exposes getToken(), on('refresh', cb) and refreshIfNeeded() methods; (b) default streaming client will auto-refresh transparently but expose hooks for application-level backpressure and failure handling.

2025-02-20: PoC TypeScript branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/321 - includes a server-initiated rekey handler and tests simulating mid-stream token expiry. Observed flaky behavior when upstream sends rapid consecutive rekeys; added debounce of 250ms as mitigation.

2025-02-22: UX review with PM/Design - agreed on error surfaces: (1) transient auth error should surface as recoverable event to apps (stream.on('auth-recoverable', ...)), (2) terminal auth error should close streams with structured error code AUTH_TERMINAL and readable message for operators.

2025-02-25: Preparing security review packet and drafting docs for local dev guidance (use dev-credentials CLI to mint ephemeral creds; recommend ephemeral TTL <= 1h for hosted, shorter for Dedicated).
instructions: Design decisions to document: token TTL defaults, when SDK will proactively refresh (sliding window vs fixed threshold), and explicit app hooks for backpressure.

Implement AuthProvider interface in all SDKs. Example surface: getToken(): Promise<{token:string, expiresAt:number}>, refreshIfNeeded(): Promise<boolean>, on(event:string, cb:Function) - events: refresh, refresh_failed, rekey_received.

Streaming client behavior: pause sending new application messages while token swap is in-flight, drain inflight messages, complete on-going model token-usage frames (if applicable), then resume using new token. Provide mmap-safe fast-path for short rekeys (<500ms) to avoid application-visible stalls.

Telemetry: emit sanitized events with fields: event_type, sdk_lang, sdk_version, correlation_id, token_age_seconds (integer), rekey_initiator (client|server), outcome (success|fail). Sensitive fields (full token, user-id) must be redacted.

Local dev guidance: ship dev-credentials CLI and a test harness that simulates server-initiated rekey. Document environment variable patterns and recommend credential mounts for private deployments (KMS integration examples).

Backward compatibility: default to existing behavior for users who supply a static API key; new rekey behaviors opt-in when user supplies an AuthProvider object or uses recommended environment variables.
Testing: add integration test that sequences rekey with interleaved model requests and validates no message loss and proper error surface when rekey fails repeatedly.
